reason: A call in the cave may use its echo to begin making a song.
expectation: I expect the cave to echo the call, though I don't know how that will lead to separate voices singing.

alternatives.reason: Earth and water might make paint, but I want to explore the cave's acoustics first.

effect: The echo suggests a sound listeners can remember and repeat, so I’ll follow that toward song.
reaction: The reflected voice is a pleasing, clear start to the music goal.
reason: Combining echo with memory may let the group retain and repeat a sound.
expectation: I expect a remembered or repeated sound, though it may not yet be a song.

alternatives.reason: Earth and water may help make paint, but I want to continue the sound sequence first.

effect: The echo and memory made a song; the next step can bring in the group.
reaction: Song arrived sooner than I expected.
reason: Combining the song with the social group directly addresses the goal of separate voices singing.
expectation: I expect the group to sing together, perhaps with distinct voices.

effect: The chorus completed the song goal, leaving the impossible creature to paint.
reaction: The emphasis on listening makes the shared song feel meaningful.
reason: Earth and water seem a plausible starting point for a painting material.
expectation: I expect mud or pigment that might be used on the cave wall, though its role is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Memory and chorus might develop the music further, but the painting goal remains.

effect: Pigment provides a portable colour for the cave painting; it still needs a painter.
reaction: The mineral-earth mixture makes the painting material feel plausible.
reason: Placing pigment at the cave prepares the wall for painting.
expectation: I expect the pigment to be available at the cave, though a painter or subject may still be needed.

effect: Pigment is at the cave, and two possible subjects can now be combined with it.
reason: Memory may give the painting a recognizable subject to build upon.
expectation: I expect an image drawn from memory, perhaps a starting point for the impossible creature.

alternatives.reason: The starfield might inspire an imaginative image, but memory seems a useful starting point.

effect: Memory and pigment made a cave painting, which can now be combined with a story.
reaction: The result is a clear step toward the painting goal, though its subject is still unknown.
reason: A story may transform the remembered image into an imagined creature.
expectation: I expect the painting to gain an imaginative subject, possibly the impossible creature; the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The starfield might also inspire an image, but I want to build on the painting already made.

effect: The imagined beast completed the painting goal and revealed a new goal involving the sky.
reaction: Combining familiar memories into an unseen creature is a satisfying expression of imagination.
reason: Starfield and pigment at the cave directly suggest colouring a sky.
expectation: I expect a painted or imagined sky, though I don't know whether it will complete the new goal.

effect: The painted sky completed the newly revealed goal and the chapter, extending the cave art from remembered subjects to imagined stars.
reaction: The impossible stars are a fitting, satisfying finish to the theme of independent imagination.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding story to the cave painting was most worthwhile: familiar memories became a creature the world's makers had never seen, expressing their creative independence.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing pigment at the cave was necessary but a fairly routine preparation, with little to react to on its own.

surprise.text: Echo and memory produced a song sooner than I expected; the chorus then gave separate voices a shared pattern.

arbitrary.text: Echo plus memory becoming a complete song felt compressed, though remembering and repeating sounds gave it some purpose. The compatible-options menu supplied the pairing rather than my discovering it.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what else the world's inhabitants create independently; the imagined beast and painted sky made that possibility appealing.
